key_insight: FAMOSE uses the ReAct (reasoning + acting) paradigm to autonomously generate, evaluate, and select informative features for tabular data, substantially reducing the need for manual feature engineering while improving downstream performance.
problem_solved: Automates the hard, expertise-heavy search over an exponentially large feature space to discover high-quality features for tabular ML tasks, integrating generation, evaluation, and selection into one loop.
method: ReAct agent loop: alternate reasoning (propose feature transformations) and acting (apply transformations to data) to explore candidate features.
Model-in-the-loop evaluation: iteratively evaluate candidates with predictive models and scoring metrics, pruning and refining proposals.
Integrated selection and optimization: combine feature importance, redundancy checks, and resource-aware search to produce a compact, high-performing feature set.
impact: Reduces time and domain expertise required for tabular feature engineering, improving reproducibility and enabling practitioners to achieve stronger models with less manual effort.
visual_elements: Pipeline diagram of the ReAct loop (Reason → Act → Evaluate → Select) showing data flowing through generation and model evaluation stages.
Before vs. after bar chart of model performance (e.g., accuracy or AUC) with baseline features vs. FAMOSE-augmented features.
Feature search-space visualization (tree or heatmap) showing pruning of candidates and convergence to a compact feature set.
Icon set: dataset/table icon, robot/agent icon, score/metric gauge, and a checklist representing selected features.
paper_title: FAMOSE: A ReAct Approach to Automated Feature Discovery
paper_authors: Keith Burghardt, Jienan Liu, Sadman Sakib, Yuning Hao, Bo Li
